{"class": "fixable",
 "chokepoint": [{"operator": "page reads of orders table B-tree via async I/O",
                 "component": "asynchronous I/O layer",
                 "frozen": true,
                 "why_every_version_executes_it": "No index on price_cents, so every version must read all orders leaf pages to find the top 10.",
                 "least_work": {"amount": 4394, "unit": "pages", "per_unit_cost_us": 2.0,
                                "total_ms": 8.8,
                                "calling_context": "warm page cache, sequential single-pass scan, large batched reads"},
                 "max_cores": 1}],
 "floor_ms": 8.8,
 "L_delta": -3.66,
 "rationale": "The only frozen work is reading about 4.4k pages, roughly 9 ms, far below T_R_upper (341 ms). The cost is in mutable code: Turso's sorter builds a record for every row and fully sorts all 300k rows (op_make_record, quicksort). Replacing this with a top-N sorter for ORDER BY ... LIMIT, keeping only 10 rows as SQLite does, is an admissible VDBE/sorter change. Start-up overhead is about 4 ms. The gap is fixable."}
